diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here, $\mathcal{M}_{\rm root}$ collects all cyclotomic factors with even exponents (a perfect square) and $\mathcal{M}_{\rm rad}$ collects the square-free part ($e_d \in \{-1,0,1\}$ for all $d$).
In the cyclotomic monomial representation, square roots are handled exactly at the exponent level, avoiding algebraic field extensions during compilation.

issues.failure_explanation: The decomposition $\mathcal{M}_{\rm geom}=\mathcal{M}_{\rm root}\cdot\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_{\rm rad}}$ only isolates the perfect-square part; the residual $\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_{\rm rad}}$ has a square-free exponent vector ($e_d\in\{-1,0,1\}$), so the root cannot be expressed with integer exponents and is deferred to evaluation, not 'resolved at the exponent level'. Evaluating $\sqrt{\Pi_{\mathbb{T}}(\mathcal{M}_{\rm rad})}$ in an exact target field $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{2h})$ generally requires adjoining a square root — a quadratic field extension — unless the radicand happens to be a square in $\mathbb{T}$. Concrete counterexample: the triangle coefficient $\Delta_{111}$ at $q=e^{i\pi/6}$ ($h=6$) equals $\sqrt{1/[4]_q}$ with $[4]_q=\sin(4\pi/6)/\sin(\pi/6)=\sqrt{3}$, i.e. $3^{-1/4}\notin\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_6)=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$. The paper's own first sentence correctly scopes the benefit to compilation ('during compilation'), and the algorithm's final step silently presupposes that $\mathbb{T}$ contains the root; the blanket 'without field extension' promise is therefore false for exact evaluation in general.

failure_location.quote: The entire square root is resolved at the exponent level, without field extension and without any polynomial computation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the compilation stage: state that the square root is isolated at the exponent level into a square-free residual, and that evaluation requires the target field to contain $\sqrt{\Pi_{\mathbb{T}}(\mathcal{M}_{\rm rad})}$, adjoining a quadratic extension when it does not.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised exact, extension-free square-root capability is withdrawn for general amplitudes with odd cyclotomic exponents: exact projection must adjoin square roots (quadratic extensions) in general. The DCR definition, both algorithms, and all complexity and numerical claims survive, and the 6j benchmark's combined four-triangle prefactor happens to land in the cyclotomic field (consistent with the working exact benchmarks), so no labelled result is invalidated.
issues.title: Square-root capability claimed as fully resolved at exponent level 'without field extension', which is false at evaluation
issues.why_classification: A contained clarification restores accuracy: the compilation-time benefits (integer-exponent square extraction, no dense polynomial arithmetic) are untouched, both algorithms remain correct, and all reported benchmarks and complexity bounds survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The intrinsic sensitivity of the problem is governed by the condition number (Eq.~\eqref{eq:condition_num}), which is independent of representation.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition number $\kappa=\sum_z|T_z|/|S|$ measures cancellation between the summands of the alternating sum. Algebraic reduction of each summand — the DCR's exact cancellation of numerator/denominator cyclotomic factors — leaves every $|T_z|$ unchanged and therefore leaves $\kappa$ unchanged; the between-summand cancellation is necessarily realized in the final numerical summation. The claim that the $\kappa$-cancellations 'are no longer realized numerically, but are instead resolved exactly at the algebraic level' is thus false. What the DCR actually achieves is exact within-summand cancellation, which compresses the per-term dynamic range (the representation-induced factor $\gamma_{\rm rep}$) and improves per-term accuracy, while the intrinsic $\mathcal{O}(\kappa Z\epsilon)$ term in the paper's own error model remains and ultimately dominates: the tables show $\gamma_{\rm DCR}=862.8$ still exceeding $\log_{10}\kappa=58.12$ by more than an order of magnitude at $j=400$, and DCR Float64 still fails at $k=500$, $j=110$ with $\approx 433\%$ relative error ($1.5083\times10^{-3}$ vs truth $2.8290\times10^{-4}$) — the same intrinsic failure mode, merely delayed.

failure_location.quote: In particular, the large intermediate cancellations to resolve the condition number $\kappa$ in Section~\ref{subsec:cancellation} are no longer realized numerically, but are instead resolved exactly at the algebraic level.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reframe the stability claim: the DCR performs exact within-summand cancellation and compresses per-term dynamic range, reducing the representation-induced amplification $\gamma_{\rm rep}$, while the intrinsic condition-number error $\mathcal{O}(\kappa Z\epsilon)$ — representation-independent — remains as the achievable-accuracy floor; the DCR delays, but does not remove, catastrophic cancellation.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised stability mechanism is weaker than stated: the DCR delays but cannot eliminate catastrophic cancellation, and the abstract's 'reducing cancellation-induced error amplification' narrative, the 'algebraic preconditioner' interpretation, and the title's 'Stable ... Evaluation' promise must be read as dynamic-range compression plus delayed (not resolved) intrinsic failure. No labelled formal result (prop:cyclo_fact, prop:deformation_as_evaluation, prop:admissibility, thm:added-1, prop:added-1) is invalidated, and the memory/complexity benchmarks remain valid.
issues.title: Claim that the DCR resolves the condition-number cancellation exactly at the algebraic level is false; only within-summand cancellation is exact
issues.why_classification: The repair is a conceptual reframing needing no new proof architecture: the formal results, the compilation complexity claims, and the empirical benchmarks (compressed $\gamma$, delayed sign errors, linear memory) all survive. However, the advertised guarantee type changes materially, from 'the condition-number cancellation is resolved exactly' to 'representation-induced amplification is reduced while the intrinsic $\kappa$-limit is intact', so it is more than a minor local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\mathbb{T}$ be the target field and $C_{\mathbb{T}}$ the cost of one arithmetic operation in $\mathbb{T}$. Then evaluation cost of the DCR requires
\mathcal{O}\!\left( D_{\max} \cdot C_{\mathbb{T}} + Z \cdot K \cdot S_{\max} \cdot C_{\mathbb{T}} \right)
Let $Z = z_{\max} - z_{\min}$ denote the summation length and $D_{\max}$ the maximal cyclotomic order appearing in the factorization.

issues.failure_explanation: The loop body recomputes $\Pi_{\mathbb{T}}(\mathcal{M}_{\rm base})$ at every one of the $Z$ iterations. Because $\mathcal{M}_{\rm base}$ contains a factorial like $[z_{\min}+1]_q!$, whose exponent vector has $\lfloor (z_{\min}+1)/d\rfloor\ge 1$ for all $d\le z_{\min}+1$, its support is $\Theta(D_{\max})$ and each evaluation costs $\Theta(D_{\max}\cdot C_{\mathbb{T}})$. As written, the procedure therefore costs $\Theta(Z\cdot D_{\max}\cdot C_{\mathbb{T}})$ — e.g. $\mathcal{O}(j^2)$ for the symmetric $6j$-symbol, where $Z\sim j$ and $D_{\max}\sim j$ — contradicting the $\mathcal{O}(D_{\max}\cdot C_{\mathbb{T}} + Z\cdot K\cdot S_{\max}\cdot C_{\mathbb{T}})$ evaluation bound of Proposition prop:added-1 that the algorithm is presented to realize. The returned value is correct; only the cost guarantee fails as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Hoist the loop-invariant: compute $v_{\rm base}\gets\Pi_{\mathbb{T}}(\mathcal{M}_{\rm base})$ once before the loop and replace the in-loop recomputation with $S_{\rm sum}\gets S_{\rm sum} + v_{\rm base}\cdot R$. This restores the stated bound with no other change.
issues.overall_effect: An implementation following the published procedure literally would be slower by a factor of $D_{\max}$ than the near-linear (in $Z$) evaluation scaling claimed in Proposition prop:added-1 and used in the latency discussion. The proposition's bound itself remains valid for an optimal implementation, so no formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: Projection algorithm recomputes Pi_T(M_base) inside the loop, violating the stated O(D_max + Z*K*S_max) evaluation bound
issues.why_classification: A one-line local repair (hoisting an invariant) preserves the algorithm's correctness, the stated complexity bound, and every dependent claim, with no new construction or reoptimization required.
